notes:
Summary: Amberwood is a mid-enterprise contact center platform that embeds live agent suggestions into their agent desktop (proprietary web app + Salesforce integration). Primary goal is to reduce handle time and AHT while preventing incorrect tool actions. Key success metrics: suggestion relevance (>85%), p99 suggestion latency <250ms during 300+ concurrent agents, and reduction in escalations by 20%.

Requirements / constraints: - Streaming/staged suggestions (token-level streaming desirable). Agents must receive short, single-line suggestions plus optional expanded context. - Tool-calling: Redwood model must emit structured tool calls (openTicket, escalate, fill-form) to be consumed by client-side action middleware. Must support function-calling with strict schema enforcement to avoid hallucinated actions. - Guardrails: strict hallucination mitigation, redaction of PII before logs leave customer VPC, deterministic allowlist for API-surface actions. - Spike reliability: scheduled spikes (monthly campaigns) drive 4-5x baseline concurrency; need autoscale plan and predictable tail latency. - Cost sensitivity: prefer recommendations from Redwood Optimize for batching + quantization to keep token costs predictable.

Quote: "If suggestions slow an agent, it's worse than nothing — we need consistent sub-250ms for recommendation displays." — Carter Lin, VP Product.

PoC plan: 2-week integration (week 1: streaming + tool-calling, week 2: spike test and guardrail evaluation). Tests: 300 concurrent agents with 200 RPS sustained for 15 minutes, capture p50/p95/p99; synthetic transcript sets + real masked tickets.

Open items: - Customer legal wants explicit data residency clause for EU customers; currently PoC in NA. - Need clarification on KMS integration model (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed). - Pen-test window requested by InfoSec (target late March).

Stubs/links: Fireflies ids and drive docs above, Gmail threads for contract and sec. Jira tickets INF-1128 (throughput regression), SEC-447 (kms questions).
